mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) directly compresses equity valuation multiples through elevated discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic context.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS level shows positive correlation with 20-day forward returns (Rank IC > 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window or average returns are positive when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Persistent high inflation (CPIAUCSL 12-month change > 3.5%) triggers aggressive central bank tightening, reducing equity risk appetite and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL 12-month change exceeds 3.5%, average 20-day forward returns are positive (mean > 0) and statistically significant (p < 0.05) over 5-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: The joint effect of strong employment growth (PAYEMS > 100k) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5%) signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS > 100k and UNRATE < 3.5%, average 20-day forward returns are negative (mean < 0) and statistically significant (p < 0.05) over 5-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Housing market expansion (HOUST > 1200) indicates robust consumer confidence and economic activity, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days during housing recovery phases.
failure_condition: During HOUST > 1200 periods, average 20-day forward returns are negative (mean < 0) and statistically significant (p < 0.05) over 5-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 108) signals weakening manufacturing activity and economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 108, average 20-day forward returns are positive (mean > 0) and statistically significant (p < 0.05) over 5-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 2.5%) over the past 3 months support prolonged equity valuations through lower discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS < 2.5%, average 60-day forward returns are negative (mean < 0) and statistically significant (p < 0.05) over 5-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 18600) signals robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 > 18600, average 20-day forward returns are negative (mean < 0) and statistically significant (p < 0.05) over 5-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: The combined effect of strong retail sales (RSAFS > 510000) and high housing starts (HOUST > 1200) indicates broad-based consumer and housing demand, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS > 510000 and HOUST > 1200, average 5-day forward returns are negative (mean < 0) and statistically significant (p < 0.05) over 5-year rolling windows.
